title: Tax Crime and the Facilitation of Tax Evasion: Controls for Firms
summary: A nine-module programme equipping investment, wealth, fund and fintech firms to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion, detect tax crime proceeds and meet automatic exchange obligations.
intro: This training programme equips investment, wealth management, fund and fintech firms to manage tax crime risk: preventing the facilitation of tax evasion, detecting laundered tax proceeds and meeting automatic exchange of information obligations.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give compliance, financial crime and client-facing teams a practical understanding of how firms are drawn into tax crime, as a channel for laundered proceeds or as facilitators of evasion. Participants leave able to assess the firm's exposure, design reasonable prevention procedures, apply tax-aware client and investor due diligence, meet automatic exchange of information obligations and act on suspicion.
sections.What It Covers: Tax crime as a predicate offence, corporate offences of failing to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion and reasonable prevention procedures, tax evasion risk assessment and associated persons, tax-aware client due diligence and source of wealth, structures and wealth management red flags, fund structures and investor risk, automatic exchange of information under the OECD Common Reporting Standard, and suspicion, reporting and governance.
Intended Audience: MLROs, compliance officers and tax compliance teams in investment, wealth management and fund management firms
Relationship managers, private client advisers, fund administrators and transfer agency teams
Senior managers accountable for client onboarding, distribution, introducers and tax reporting
Learning Objectives: Explain tax crime as a predicate offence and how firms become channels or facilitators
Assess the firm's tax evasion facilitation risk, including through associated persons
Design reasonable prevention procedures and evidence them to supervisors and prosecutors
Apply tax-aware client and investor due diligence, including source of wealth
Recognise red flags in wealth management, structures and fund investment
Meet automatic exchange of information obligations and act on suspicion of tax crime
sections.Structure and Format: Nine modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a practitioner briefing with case studies and structure-mapping exercises, ending in a prevention procedures workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's client base and products.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, AML/CFT or client onboarding is helpful. No specialist knowledge of tax law is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
OECD, Fighting Tax Crime – The Ten Global Principles, Second Edition (2021)
OECD, Standard for Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information in Tax Matters, Second Edition (2017)
OECD, Ending the Shell Game: Cracking down on the Professionals who enable Tax and White Collar Crimes (2021)

modules.title: Tax Crime as a Financial Crime Risk
modules.summary: Why tax crimes are predicate offences for money laundering, how evasion, avoidance and laundering differ, and how investment and wealth firms become channels for the proceeds of tax crime.
objectives: Explain tax crimes as predicate offences under the FATF standards
Distinguish evasion, aggressive avoidance and laundering of tax proceeds
Identify how the firm's products and services can hold or move tax crime proceeds
syllabus: Tax crimes as designated predicate offences
Evasion, avoidance and planning: where the legal lines fall
Common schemes: undeclared income, false invoicing and hidden assets
Lessons from data leaks, enforcement cases and voluntary disclosure programmes

modules.title: Corporate Offences and Reasonable Prevention Procedures
modules.summary: How corporate offences of failing to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion work, who counts as an associated person, and what reasonable prevention procedures look like in practice.
objectives: Explain the structure of failure-to-prevent offences and the defence of reasonable procedures
Identify the firm's associated persons, including employees, agents and introducers
Design proportionate prevention procedures with clear senior management ownership
syllabus: Criminal facilitation, the corporate offence and cross-border reach
Associated persons: staff, introducers, distributors and service providers
Prevention principles: risk assessment, proportionality, commitment, due diligence, communication and monitoring
Documenting procedures and the evidence a prosecutor or supervisor would expect

modules.title: Assessing Tax Evasion Facilitation Risk
modules.summary: How to assess where the firm, its staff and associated persons could facilitate tax evasion, and how to reflect tax crime in the business-wide financial crime risk assessment.
objectives: Map facilitation risk across clients, products, jurisdictions and distribution
Assess incentives and opportunities for staff and associated persons
Integrate tax crime into the business-wide risk assessment and risk appetite
syllabus: Client, product, jurisdiction and channel risk factors
Remuneration, sales incentives and introducer arrangements
Workshops and interviews with front-line and product teams
Recording residual risk and linking it to controls

modules.title: Tax-Aware Client Due Diligence and Source of Wealth
modules.summary: How to build tax transparency into onboarding and review, from tax residence self-certifications and source of wealth to legacy clients and requests for evidence of tax compliance.
objectives: Integrate tax residence and tax compliance checks into due diligence
Assess source of wealth and source of funds for plausibility
Manage legacy and high-risk clients, including remediation and exit
syllabus: Tax residence self-certifications and reasonableness checks
Source of wealth and source of funds: evidence and plausibility
When to ask for evidence of tax compliance or regularisation
Legacy book reviews, remediation and relationship exit

modules.title: Structures, Beneficial Ownership and Wealth Management Red Flags
modules.summary: How companies, trusts, foundations and nominee arrangements are used to conceal income and assets from tax authorities, and the red flags wealth managers and advisers should recognise.
objectives: Recognise structures commonly used to conceal income and assets
Identify beneficial owners, controllers and tax-relevant persons
Apply red flags to client instructions and account activity
syllabus: Personal investment companies, trusts, foundations and nominees
Beneficial ownership, controlling persons and register limitations
Red flags: hold mail, cash, secrecy requests and unexplained transfers
Mapping exercise: unpicking a multi-layered client structure

modules.title: Fund Structures and Investor Tax Crime Risk
modules.summary: How investment funds and private market vehicles can be used to hide or round-trip untaxed money, and what fund managers, administrators and transfer agents should do about investor risk.
objectives: Identify tax crime risk in fund structures and investor flows
Apply investor due diligence across direct, nominee and omnibus holdings
Recognise red flags in subscriptions, redemptions and transfers
syllabus: Feeder, master, private and closed-ended structures: where opacity arises
Nominees, omnibus accounts, distributors and reliance on third parties
Round-tripping, side letters and unusual subscription and redemption patterns
Allocating responsibility between manager, administrator and transfer agent

modules.title: Automatic Exchange of Information and Tax Reporting
modules.summary: What automatic exchange of information under the OECD Common Reporting Standard requires of financial institutions, how arrangements to avoid it work, and how reporting extends to crypto-assets.
objectives: Explain due diligence and reporting obligations under the Common Reporting Standard
Recognise arrangements designed to avoid automatic exchange
Assess the accuracy and governance of the firm's tax reporting
syllabus: Reporting financial institutions, reportable accounts and controlling persons
Self-certification, indicia searches and change in circumstances
Avoidance arrangements, mandatory disclosure and the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework
Data quality, reconciliations, penalties and assurance over reporting

modules.title: Suspicion, Reporting and Responding to Authorities
modules.summary: How to escalate concerns about tax evasion, reach a reasoned judgement on suspicion, report to the national FIU and respond to tax authority and law enforcement requests without tipping off.
objectives: Escalate and investigate tax-related concerns consistently
Decide on and file usable suspicious activity reports involving tax crime
Handle information requests and relationship decisions correctly
syllabus: Internal reporting and whistleblowing on facilitation concerns
Suspicion of tax crime: thresholds, evidence and decision records
Report quality, tipping off and exiting or continuing relationships
Responding to tax authority, FIU and law enforcement requests

modules.title: Governance, Training and Prevention Procedures Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining governance, training and monitoring of tax crime controls, ending with a workshop in which teams test and improve the firm's prevention procedures.
objectives: Specify management information, monitoring and testing for tax crime controls
Design targeted training for staff and associated persons
Produce a gap analysis and action plan for the firm's prevention procedures
syllabus: Senior management ownership and board reporting
Training, attestations and contractual terms for associated persons
Monitoring, internal audit and periodic review of procedures
Workshop: prevention procedures gap analysis and action plan

related.title: Internal Audit in Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving internal auditors the tools to deliver risk-based assurance over the regulatory risks that matter most to boards and supervisors.

related.title: Internal Investigations and Interviewing Skills
related.summary: A nine-module programme giving control functions a structured method to investigate misconduct, whistleblowing reports and breaches, interview witnesses and subjects, and report findings.

related.title: Management and Leadership for Compliance and Risk Teams
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving managers of compliance, risk and financial crime teams the skills to lead the second line, influence the business and earn the board's confidence.

related.title: Professional Judgement and Core Skills for Compliance Staff
related.summary: A ten-module programme building the judgement, questioning, advisory and writing skills that compliance, risk and financial crime staff need to be trusted by the business, the board and the regulator.

related.title: Risk Management for Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving risk professionals the tools to design, run and evidence a risk management framework that informs decisions and withstands supervisory scrutiny.
